title: Site switch authorizes with Prospectus before the selection is stored: fail closed, reenrollment_required passed through
description:
Repo: **Papyrus**. Retitled 2026-11-14. The original design (a per-operation Prospectus authorize call in every Lambda and JS resolver behind a per-site flag, PR #948) was closed by Ryan on 2026-11-14: it was never an intentional policy decision. The ideal design authorizes ONCE at site switch and carries per-tenant role claims in the token (docs/plans/multi-tenant-architecture.md, "Shared-tier request flow", section 1, steps 3 and 4).

## What now carries the original need
- Claims in the token: PPY-0bb0fd (PR #1512, not yet merged). Tenant rules that read them: PPY-06ae68, then PPY-bdc4ee.
- Functions take the tenant from the caller: PPY-7dc463 (PR #1514 moves the first five handlers; PPY-cc8a4c merged).
- Site picker writing the TenantSelection: PPY-9619f702 (filed on the PPY-0bb0fd branch). Member removal revoking the membership and refresh tokens: PPY-9d131629 (same branch).
- Prospectus side of the check (token bound to the deployment, Account owns it, person is a member): kanbus-3e5e82, shared sign-in PPY-fdbbd7 (M4), events kanbus-6efecd (PPY-a1e75a).
- Lifecycle and standing through claims: PPY-d7274f (M7).

## The part NOT covered by any of them (this issue)
PPY-0bb0fd's trigger reads only local tables and "never Prospectus"; PPY-9619f702 refuses a pick only for lack of a local membership. No issue calls Prospectus `authorize` when a person picks or switches site, which the design note requires ("only for the deployment authorize approved"). A membership row that is stale (a missed removal event) or a standing change would otherwise still yield claims, and a Prospectus outage or a login that is no longer enrolled has no defined result.

## Outcome
A site switch (newsroom switcher and the CLI's signed-in lane) calls Prospectus `POST /v1/accounts/{id}/authorize` as the shared-tier role with the person's verified identity and the deployment, BEFORE the TenantSelection row is written and tokens are re-issued. Allowed only when `allowed` is true and the answer names the same deployment. No default tenant, ever. The token trigger is unchanged (local reads only, no Prospectus at token refresh). Briefly cached per person and deployment. One helper, two twins (`src/papyrus_content/prospectus_authorize.py`, `lib/prospectus-authorize.ts`) kept from the closed #948 design where still useful (decision parsing, ReenrollmentRequired, fixtures); no per-operation call, no feature flag, no AppSync HTTP data source, no new header on every request.

## Gherkin (features_backend/site-switch-authorize.feature)
  Scenario: A switch to a site Prospectus approves stores the selection and re-issues tokens
  Scenario: A switch Prospectus denies stores nothing and the session keeps its previous site
  Scenario: A decision for a different deployment is treated as denied
  Scenario: Prospectus unreachable denies the switch (fail closed, no silent default)
  Scenario: A login no longer enrolled reaches the CLI and console as "run papyrus login again" (reenrollment_required)
  Scenario: A stale membership row alone does not yield claims for a switch Prospectus denies
  Scenario: Token refresh never calls Prospectus

## Acceptance
Unit tests for both twins with recorded fixtures (no real ids); Behave against stubbed Prospectus answers; no sandbox. docs/cli-login.md "Authorization" and docs/multi-tenancy.md "Session claims" updated. Rollout: with the shared stack (M4), dark until PPY-9619f702 lands. Dedicated sites: the fixed tenant needs no switch; their CLI enrollment stays in epic PPY-e2a0b8.

comments.text: Ryan closed PR #948 on 2026-11-14: the per-operation design (authorize in every Lambda and JS resolver behind featureFlags.prospectusAuthorize) was never an intentional policy decision. Sorted out: the original need is carried by PPY-0bb0fd (PR #1512, role claims in the token), PPY-7dc463 (PR #1514, functions take the tenant from the caller), PPY-06ae68 and PPY-bdc4ee (rules read the claims), PPY-fdbbd7 (shared sign-in, M4), PPY-d7274f (lifecycle). PR #1513 (shared stacks, PPY-daf673) is isolation, not authorization. Not covered: the Prospectus authorize call at site switch. This issue is retitled to that remainder, reparented under PPY-fdbbd7 (M4), and the Gherkin is in the description. Per-operation calls, the feature flag and the AppSync HTTP data source are dropped.
